title: derived area and record-count totals by source feature class, maintenance-frequency code, and mowing-description text
selection: Type case-insensitively equals 'berm' or 'slootkant'; geometry and non-requested fields omitted.
geography: Provincial roads and waterways managed by the Province of Zuid-Holland, Netherlands
license: Public domain according to data.overheid.nl metadata; source catalog entry updated 2026-05-29.
limitations: Official management-object inventory, not harvested grass tonnage or verified execution. Feature areas include only objects classified as berm or slootkant; ditch banks are kept separate from road verges. Maintenance frequency is a plan/code, not a dated mowing event. No yield, collected fraction, supplier contract, wet/dry mass, contamination, storage loss, or plant-delivery record is supplied. Do not convert area to tonnes or runtime availability.
A management inventory is not proof that mowing occurred, that grass was collected, or that the object is under a GreenHub supply contract.
No biomass yield, harvested mass, dry-matter content, date-specific mowing record, contamination, storage, or delivery record is supplied.
Empty maintenance and mowing fields are preserved as empty; they are not inferred.
Only berm and slootkant feature classes are included; the latter is a separate ditch-bank stream and is not included in roadside-berm totals.
No conversion from m2 to tonnes, annual yield, nutrient load, TEA, LCA, runtime, or default input is performed.
runtime_policy: Not eligible as a feedstock quantity; use only as area/management evidence until yield, execution, collection and contract data are supplied.

fair_metadata.findable: Local URN, source ID, DataOverheid identifier, NGR UUID, layer name, and content hash are recorded.
fair_metadata.accessible: Public HTTPS WFS and catalog endpoints; source fields and exact query/filter are recorded.
fair_metadata.interoperable: UTF-8 CSV with source field names, documented square-metre units, stable feature identifiers, and separate berm/ditch-bank classes.
fair_metadata.reusable: Retrieval timestamp, filter, checksums, public-domain metadata, source limitations, and no-runtime policy are explicit.
